relationships.name: Mark Williams
relationships.notes: Lives with Sarah and is her emergency contact.

background.summary: Lives with her husband Mark and their teenage daughter; their adult son is away at university during term time.
Works part-time during term time as a teaching assistant at Bramhall Park Primary School.
background.details: Following cancer treatment she returned on a phased basis and requires the pace of return to reflect fatigue and shoulder rehabilitation.

background.summary: Previously ran five kilometres twice weekly and swam weekly.
background.details: Stopped running and swimming during treatment and currently manages shorter walks while rebuilding confidence and stamina.

background.summary: Former smoker with an estimated 7.5 pack-year history; stopped in 2018.
Reduced alcohol intake after diagnosis and currently reports approximately 10 to 14 units weekly.
Her mother developed postmenopausal breast cancer aged 68 and remains well after treatment.
background.details: No other first- or second-degree breast, ovarian, prostate or pancreatic cancer history is recorded; standard criteria did not indicate a clinical-genetics referral.

background.summary: Her father has hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
Independent with personal care, mobility and driving, without a care package.
background.details: Fatigue and right-shoulder restriction affect heavier housework, shopping and overhead tasks.

background.summary: Registered with Dr Fiona Marsh at Cheadle Hulme Medical Practice.

problem.display: Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, Stage IIA

problems.details: ER positive, PR positive, HER2 negative, Grade 2, pT2N0M0; primary treatment completed and ongoing adjuvant endocrine therapy and surveillance continue.

problem.display: Right shoulder restriction following breast surgery and radiotherapy

problems.details: Includes axillary web syndrome, scar adherence and improving restricted movement.
Improving but continues to affect work, exercise and daily activity.
Hot flushes, night sweats, sleep disruption, vaginal dryness and dyspareunia are documented.

problem.display: Fear of cancer recurrence with anxiety and low mood

problems.details: Symptoms are most prominent before appointments and contribute to poor sleep.

entries.summary: Appendicectomy performed aged 14 without complication.
Breast MDT confirmed right invasive ductal carcinoma following screening and core biopsy.
entries.outcome: Grade 2 ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma confirmed; surgery recommended.

entries.summary: Right wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy completed.

procedure.display: Right wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy

entries.outcome: Margins clear; no metastatic disease in three sentinel nodes.

entries.summary: Six cycles of adjuvant FEC-T chemotherapy completed.
entries.response: Course completed; grade 2 neutropenia, alopecia and cumulative fatigue were recorded without febrile neutropenia.

entries.summary: Adjuvant whole-breast radiotherapy and tumour-bed boost completed.
entries.indication: Post-operative treatment of Stage IIA right breast cancer.
entries.outcome: Treatment completed and rehabilitation referral made.

entries.summary: Pre-rehabilitation blood tests showed vitamin D insufficiency; other reported results were within their stated ranges.

results.referenceRange: Above 50 nmol/L sufficient; 25–50 insufficient; below 25 deficient
Below 42 normal; 42–47 pre-diabetes; 48 or above diabetes

entries.conclusion: Vitamin D was insufficient at 38 nmol/L. HbA1c was at the upper end of the normal range; the remaining reported results were within their stated reference ranges.

entries.summary: Mammography and ultrasound identified and sampled a suspicious right breast mass.

value.value: M5 mammographic mass; U5 irregular hypoechoic mass at 10 o'clock measuring 24 × 19 × 22 mm
Three morphologically normal nodes with preserved fatty hila

entries.conclusion: Highly suspicious right breast mass; ultrasound-guided core biopsy performed. Axilla sonographically normal.

entries.summary: Pre-operative MRI confirmed unifocal disease and staging CT found no distant metastasis.

value.value: Unifocal 27 mm enhancing right upper-outer-quadrant mass; no contralateral lesion or pathological nodal enhancement
No radiological evidence of distant metastatic disease

entries.conclusion: Findings supported breast-conserving surgery; clinical distant stage M0.

entries.summary: Definitive surgical histopathology established tumour type, grade, receptors, margins and pathological stage.

investigation.display: Right breast wide local excision histopathology

value.value: 28 mm invasive ductal carcinoma of no special type, Nottingham Grade 2

entries.conclusion: Grade 2 ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma, pT2N0M0, Stage IIA, completely excised.

entries.summary: Three-visit oncology physiotherapy assessment documented improving right shoulder movement, strength and axillary cording.
entries.outcome: Right active flexion improved 130° to 148° to 158°; abduction 110° to 132° to 146°; external rotation 45° to 55° to 62°. Internal rotation improved from sacrum to L3 to L1. Residual guarded end-range movement and scapular dyskinesis remained.
components: Left comparison at visit 3: flexion 172°, abduction 168°, external rotation 80°, internal rotation T7
Visit 3 strength: flexors 4/5, abductors 4/5, external rotators 4-/5, internal rotators 4+/5; visit 1 was 3+/5 globally
Grip strength: right 22 kg, left 27 kg
Scar healed without infection or breakdown; medial scar remained adherent with reduced glide
Axillary web syndrome improved from a visible cord extending to the medial elbow to a faint residual palpable band
Marked visit-1 scapular hitching and trunk compensation was much reduced, but delayed upward rotation persisted under load

entries.summary: Holistic pain assessment distinguished musculoskeletal scar and chest-wall pain from neuropathic-type axillary and medial-arm symptoms.
entries.outcome: Pain was 3/10 at rest, 5–6/10 with reaching or lifting, with brief sharp catches up to 7/10. Chest-wall pain was tight, aching and pulling; axillary and medial-arm symptoms were burning, tingling and numb in the intercostobrachial nerve distribution.
components: Present most days since surgery and worse late in the working day and after driving
Aggravated by overhead reach, carrying, tight bra straps, prolonged driving and light contact over the altered-sensation area
Relieved by rest, arm support, avoiding overhead reach, warmth, gentle scar massage and ibuprofen
Ibuprofen helped the aching component more than the tingling component

entries.summary: Occupational Therapy reviewed personal and instrumental daily activities and return-to-work function.
entries.outcome: Independent in personal care, stairs, mobility and local driving, but right shoulder restriction and fatigue affected washing hair, upper-body dressing, longer driving, carrying, housework, overhead tasks and work duties.

entries.summary: Consent-based holistic review documented fear of recurrence, body-image concerns and tamoxifen-associated sexual symptoms.
entries.outcome: Mood fluctuated with fatigue and appointments; persistent fear of recurrence affected sleep. Sarah denied self-harm or suicidal thoughts. Vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, reduced libido and body-image concerns affected intimacy with her husband.
components: Checks for lumps most weeks and experiences increased anxiety before appointments
Avoids looking at her chest while changing and avoids swimming costumes and vest tops in public
Declined psychology referral at this review but agreed it could be revisited
Vaginal symptoms began about six weeks after tamoxifen; occasional water-based lubricant had provided limited support
Regular vaginal moisturiser and lubricant advice supplied; specialist menopause-in-cancer or psychosexual referral offered
Sarah wished to consider referral and received direct CNS self-referral details

entries.summary: Review documented good regular-medicine adherence but low confidence and inconsistent rehabilitation exercise.
entries.outcome: Aware but struggling: Sarah understood the intended rehabilitation behaviours but had difficulty sustaining them independently. Walking improved, but her home shoulder programme remained less frequent than prescribed because of fatigue and fear of lymphoedema.
components: Visit 1 goal: daily shoulder exercises on most days for four weeks; partially achieved at 2–3 times weekly
Visit 2 goals: discuss exercise beliefs and walk 20 minutes four times weekly; walking achieved but the belief persisted
No visit 3 goal was yet agreed because setting the new SMART goal was reserved for the learning activity
Phased work goal was a return to contracted hours by September 2026, paced with Sarah rather than fixed by the employer

entries.title: Post-operative histology and staging letter
entries.summary: Breast surgeon wrote to primary care with final histology, staging and the oncology referral plan.
entries.body: Dear Dr Marsh, final histopathology after right wide local excision confirms a 28 mm Grade 2 invasive ductal carcinoma with clear margins and no metastatic disease in three sentinel nodes. The tumour is ER and PR positive and HER2 negative, with final stage pT2N0M0, Stage IIA. The Breast MDT recommends Clinical Oncology review for adjuvant treatment. The wound is healing well and Sarah has received shoulder-mobility advice and Breast Care CNS contact details.

entries.title: Completion of chemotherapy and radiotherapy plan
entries.summary: Clinical Oncology updated primary care after chemotherapy and before radiotherapy.
entries.body: Dear Dr Marsh, Sarah has completed six cycles of adjuvant FEC-T chemotherapy. Expected toxicities included grade 2 neutropenia, alopecia and cumulative fatigue, without febrile neutropenia. She is fit to proceed to right-breast radiotherapy. After radiotherapy she will start tamoxifen 20 mg daily and will be referred for shoulder, functional and holistic rehabilitation.

entries.title: End-of-treatment rehabilitation referral
entries.summary: The Breast Care CNS referred Sarah for multidisciplinary rehabilitation.
entries.body: Dear colleagues, Sarah completed radiotherapy on 30 January 2026. Her Holistic Needs Assessment identified fatigue, right shoulder stiffness, anxiety about recurrence, menopausal symptoms and practical concerns about returning to work. She consented to referral and information sharing for physiotherapy, occupational therapy and ongoing CNS support.

author.name: Sandra Whitfield
author.service: Jean McFarlane Trust Breast Care Team

entries.title: Request for advice on menopausal symptom management
entries.summary: Primary care requested oncology advice about tamoxifen-associated symptoms.
entries.body: Dear Dr Chandran, Sarah reports worsening hot flushes, night sweats, sleep disruption, low mood, vaginal dryness and dyspareunia since starting tamoxifen. Non-hormonal options have been discussed and HRT has been advised against. Please advise on oncology-specific management and appropriate specialist support, and share the concern with the rehabilitation team.

entries.title: Initial oncology physiotherapy assessment
entries.summary: Physiotherapy documented shoulder restriction, axillary web syndrome and the rehabilitation plan.
entries.body: Dear Dr Marsh, initial assessment found restricted right shoulder flexion and abduction, pain at end range, axillary web syndrome and adherent scar tissue. Sarah was avoiding exercise because she feared provoking lymphoedema. Evidence-based education was provided and a graded programme of cording release, scar mobilisation, range-of-motion work and strengthening was started.

entries.title: Occupational therapy functional review
entries.summary: Occupational Therapy documented functional limitations and recommended a paced return to work.
entries.body: Dear Dr Marsh, Sarah remains on a phased return of three mornings weekly and reports pressure for a fixed full-time return date. Fatigue and shoulder restriction continue to affect overhead and sustained tasks. Occupational Health referral and temporary workplace adjustments are recommended while rehabilitation continues, with the return paced to clinical readiness.

entries.title: Breast Care CNS rehabilitation review
entries.summary: CNS completed the third holistic rehabilitation review.
entries.body: Physical progress is good, but fear of recurrence remains prominent before appointments. Tamoxifen-associated vaginal dryness and dyspareunia were discussed with consent; written advice and a psychosexual self-referral route were offered. Sleep remains disrupted by vasomotor symptoms and rumination. Continue rehabilitation and consider psychology or psychosexual referral if concerns persist.

entries.title: Senior oncology physiotherapy review
entries.summary: Physiotherapy recorded improving movement with continuing exercise concerns.
entries.body: Right shoulder movement and cording have improved substantially since the first visit. Home exercises are still completed less often than prescribed because of concern about lymphoedema. Measurement trends were used to reinforce safe progressive activity. Progress to resisted strengthening and review for community exercise discharge.

entries.title: Occupational therapy rehabilitation review
entries.summary: Occupational Therapy reviewed function and the unresolved return-to-work plan.
entries.body: Sarah remains on three mornings weekly and continues to face pressure for a fixed full-time return date. Overhead and heavy tasks remain limited, and low mood is linked to reduced contribution at home. Pacing and graded occupational demand were reviewed. Await Occupational Health and contact the school with consent to reinforce a clinically paced return.

catalogue.synopsis: An adult completing multidisciplinary rehabilitation after treatment for breast cancer, with durable oncology correspondence and professional rehabilitation notes.
